classification.difficultyReason: Use the power-of-a-power law to establish equivalent exponential rules, then transfer the known decreasing graph and its key features.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use the index laws to explain why $y=\left(\frac12\right)^x$ has the same graph as $y=2^{-x}$.

answer.short: $\left(\frac12\right)^x=(2^{-1})^x=2^{-x}$, so the two rules give the same value for every $x$.
answer.worked:
Since $\frac12=2^{-1}$, the power-of-a-power law gives
$$\begin{align*}\left(\frac12\right)^x&=(2^{-1})^x\\\left(\frac12\right)^x&=2^{-x}.\end{align*}$$
The rules therefore define the same function and have the same graph.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence sketch the graph of the function $y=\left(\frac12\right)^x$.

answer.short: A decreasing exponential through $(-1,2)$ and $(0,1)$, with horizontal asymptote $y=0$.
answer.worked: By part a, this is the graph of $y=2^{-x}$. It passes through $(-1,2)$ and $(0,1)$ and decreases towards the horizontal asymptote $y=0$ as $x\to\infty$. Draw a smooth curve above the $x$-axis.
